summary: Noémie Verdon specializes in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.

Noël Péri (1865–1922) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo Fine Arts School (1896–1906), founded Mélanges japonais in 1904, and served at École française d'Extrême-Orient as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911).
Nyak Shul Khenpo Gyurmé Ösal studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon, under Nyanatiloka Mahathera (1937), and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953). He co-founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as leader/editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).
Nyingcha Duoji is a Tibetologist who studied at Boston University and Harvard University, earning his PhD attested in 2014 under Mark Elliott and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche (~1855–1887) and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Terton Sogyal, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nyoshul Monastery (~1944–1955) and Katok Monastery, learning under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Octave Hamelin (1856–1907) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Henri-IV. He held posts at École Normale Supérieure (~1881–1884), the University of Bordeaux (~1884–1905), and the University of Paris (~1905–1907).

Ogyen Trinley Dorje (born 1985) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (~2000–2023), Bokar Rinpoche (~2000–2004), the 14th Dalai Lama (~2000), Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Pema Donyo Nyinje.

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1945), the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969), and the University of Jena.

Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Pennsylvania and Freiburg (Dr. phil. 1993), and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–1999), Pennsylvania (1989), Munich (professor, 2008), and EPHE (2016).

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (~2003–2009) under the supervision of Ernst Steinkellner.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After degrees at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, he directed the Albright Institute (1953) and held professorships at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and IAS (1990–1998).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) studied Indology and Buddhism at University of Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede and Betty Heimann. He became Sanskrit department head at Ceylon (1943) and held visiting roles at Pennsylvania, Harvard, and Smith.
Oliver Hellwig works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and held a post at the University of Zurich attested in 2024–2025.
Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1939). He taught at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).
Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant and has served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.
